exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal vs. caesarean section)
cohort: 90 neonates with positive blood cultures for sepsis, admitted to the NICU ward of Mustafa Khomeini Hospital in Tehran, Iran, from 2007 to 2014
finding: Staphylococcus aureus and E. coli were the most common pathogens in neonatal sepsis cases, with varying resistance rates to common antibiotics, emphasizing the importance of regional resistance pattern monitoring.
mod_finding: Neonates delivered via cesarean section had a higher rate of sepsis caused by Staphylococcus aureus and E. coli compared to those delivered vaginally.
